question: A can do 1/4 part of a work in 9 days. B can do 2/3 part of the same work in 28 days. Working together, in how many days can A and B complete the whole work ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time for A = 9 × 4 = 36 days

Total time for B = 28 × (3/2) = 42 days

Required time (A+B) = (36 × 42) / (36 + 42)

⇒ (36 × 42) / 78 = (6 × 42) / 13 = 252/13 days

**∴ The correct answer is 252/13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Time for 1/4 work by A = 9 days

Time for 2/3 work by B = 28 days

Calculations:

⇒ Total time for A to finish work = 9 × 4 = 36 days

⇒ Total time for B to finish work = 28 × (3/2) = 14 × 3 = 42 days

⇒ Total Work = LCM(36, 42) = 252 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 7 + 6 = 13 units/day

⇒ Time taken by (A + B) together = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Time = 252/13 days

**∴ The correct answer is 252/13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

If A can do a work in 'x' days and B can do it in 'y' days, then together they can do it in (x × y) / (x + y) days.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Work done is directly proportional to efficiency and time (W = E × T). For a constant work, efficiency is inversely proportional to time (E ∝ 1/T).

Fractional Work Rule

If a person completes a/b part of work in D days, the time taken to complete the full work (1 unit) is D × (b/a) days.</p
